title: Cell Cycle and Cell Division
seo_title: Cell Cycle and Cell Division Class 11 Biology Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 10)
standard_code: Class 11 Biology, Chapter 10: Cell Cycle and Cell Division
standard_text: Cell cycle, mitosis, meiosis and their significance.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division: interphase, the stages of mitosis, cytokinesis, meiosis I and II, crossing over and chromosome numbers. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Mitosis keeps the chromosome number; meiosis halves it.
body_html:
How to think about it

The cell cycle has interphase (G₁ growth, S DNA replication, G₂ preparation) and the M phase (mitosis and cytokinesis). Mitosis has prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase; it gives two identical diploid cells for growth and repair.

Meiosis has two divisions: meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes (reductional) after crossing over in pachytene; meiosis II separates sister chromatids. It forms four haploid cells and creates variation.

Example

Phase when DNA doubles?

synthesis

Answer: S phase

Example

2n = 46. Gamete?

halved

Answer: 23

Common mistakes

  • Saying the chromosome number doubles in S phase.
  • Putting crossing over in metaphase.
  • Calling meiosis II reductional.

faq.q: What is the difference between mitosis and meiosis?
faq.a: Mitosis gives two diploid cells identical to the parent; meiosis gives four haploid cells that differ genetically.
In pachytene of prophase I, between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.

items.q: Which of these is an event of interphase?
items.e: “Synthesis of proteins for division” is an event of interphase.

items.q: Which of these is an event of prophase I of meiosis?
items.e: “Crossing over” is an event of prophase I of meiosis.

items.q: What happens in prophase?
c: DNA replicates and the amount of DNA doubles
chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form
nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes
the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles
items.e: Prophase: chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form.

items.q: Which of these is an event of mitotic anaphase?
c: sister chromatids moving to opposite poles
items.e: “Sister chromatids moving to opposite poles” is an event of mitotic anaphase.

items.q: How long does a typical human cell cycle take in culture?
items.e: Yeast takes only about 90 minutes.

items.q: Which of these is an event of interphase?
items.e: “DNA replication” is an event of interphase.

items.q: What is the G₀ phase?
c: a quiescent stage where cells stop dividing but stay metabolically active
items.e: e.g. heart cells.

items.q: What happens in telophase?
c: proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing
DNA replicates and the amount of DNA doubles
the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles
nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes
items.e: Telophase: nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes.

items.q: Which of these is NOT an event of telophase?
items.e: “Synthesis of proteins for division” is not an event of telophase; the other three are.

items.q: Which division is called reductional division?
items.e: The chromosome number is halved.

items.q: In which stage of the cell cycle does this happen: chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form?
items.e: Prophase: chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form.

items.q: In which stage of the cell cycle does this happen: the cytoplasm divides to form two daughter cells?
items.e: Cytokinesis: the cytoplasm divides to form two daughter cells.

items.q: Which of these is NOT an event of interphase?
c: sister chromatids moving to opposite poles
items.e: “Sister chromatids moving to opposite poles” is not an event of interphase; the other three are.

items.q: What is the significance of mitosis?
c: growth, repair and keeping the chromosome number the same
creating genetic variation by crossing over
items.e: It replaces worn-out cells.

items.q: What happens in G₁ phase?
c: chromosomes line up at the equator (metaphase plate)
nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes
the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles
the cell grows but its DNA does not replicate
items.e: G₁ phase: the cell grows but its DNA does not replicate.

items.q: Which of these is an event of telophase?
items.e: “Reappearance of the nucleolus” is an event of telophase.

items.q: Which cells keep dividing throughout life in plants?
items.e: e.g. root and shoot tips.

items.q: At which stage are chromosomes best studied?
items.e: They are most condensed then.

items.q: Which of these is NOT an event of telophase?
items.e: “Growth of the cell” is not an event of telophase; the other three are.

items.q: What happens in anaphase?
c: the cytoplasm divides to form two daughter cells
chromosomes line up at the equator (metaphase plate)
the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles
the cell grows but its DNA does not replicate
items.e: Anaphase: the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles.

items.q: What happens to the DNA content in the S phase?
items.e: The chromosome number stays 2n.

items.q: What happens in cytokinesis?
c: the cell grows but its DNA does not replicate
nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes
proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing
the cytoplasm divides to form two daughter cells
items.e: Cytokinesis: the cytoplasm divides to form two daughter cells.

items.q: In which stage of the cell cycle does this happen: the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles?
items.e: Anaphase: the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles.

items.q: Which division is called equational division?
items.e: The chromosome number stays the same.

items.q: In a root tip squash, 18 of 500 cells are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
items.e: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells × 100 = 3.6%.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 24 hours. In a sample, 30 of 240 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 30/240 × 1,440 min = 180 min.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 24 hours. In a sample, 12 of 150 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 12/150 × 1,440 min = 115 min.

items.q: In a root tip squash, 24 of 200 cells are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
items.e: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells × 100 = 12%.

items.q: In a root tip squash, 36 of 240 cells are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
items.e: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells × 100 = 15%.

items.q: Which enzyme helps crossing over?
items.e: Crossing over is between non-sister chromatids.

items.q: What forms the spindle in animal cells?
items.e: Plant cells form a spindle without centrioles.

items.q: What happens in S phase?
c: chromosomes line up at the equator (metaphase plate)
the cytoplasm divides to form two daughter cells
nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes
DNA replicates and the amount of DNA doubles
items.e: S phase: DNA replicates and the amount of DNA doubles.

items.q: What happens in G₂ phase?
c: proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing
the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles
nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes
chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form
items.e: G₂ phase: proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing.

items.q: In which stage of the cell cycle does this happen: proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing?
items.e: G₂ phase: proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing.

items.q: What is the significance of meiosis?
c: it halves the chromosome number for gametes and creates variation
items.e: Fertilisation restores the diploid number.

items.q: In a root tip squash, 18 of 240 cells are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
items.e: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells × 100 = 7.5%.

items.q: In a root tip squash, 18 of 250 cells are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
items.e: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells × 100 = 7.2%.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 16 hours. In a sample, 12 of 250 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 12/250 × 960 min = 46.1 min.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 18 hours. In a sample, 12 of 200 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 12/200 × 1,080 min = 64.8 min.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 12 hours. In a sample, 24 of 400 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 24/400 × 720 min = 43.2 min.

items.q: What happens in diakinesis of meiosis?
c: the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata are seen
chromosomes become visible as thin threads
chiasmata terminalise and the nuclear envelope breaks down
homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together
items.e: Diakinesis: chiasmata terminalise and the nuclear envelope breaks down.

items.q: In which stage of meiosis does this happen: chiasmata terminalise and the nuclear envelope breaks down?
items.e: Diakinesis: chiasmata terminalise and the nuclear envelope breaks down.

items.q: Which of these is NOT an event of interphase?
items.e: “Synapsis of homologous chromosomes” is not an event of interphase; the other three are.

items.q: In which stage of meiosis does this happen: sister chromatids separate as the centromere splits?
items.e: Anaphase II: sister chromatids separate as the centromere splits.

items.q: In which stage of meiosis does this happen: homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together?
items.e: Anaphase I: homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together.

items.q: Which of these is an event of prophase I of meiosis?
c: sister chromatids moving to opposite poles
items.e: “Synapsis of homologous chromosomes” is an event of prophase I of meiosis.

items.q: Which of these is an event of interphase?
items.e: “Duplication of the centriole” is an event of interphase.

items.q: What is the longest phase of meiosis I prophase in oocytes of some vertebrates?
c: diplotene, which can last months or years
items.e: Oocytes stay in diplotene for a long time.

items.q: Which of these is an event of mitotic anaphase?
items.e: “Splitting of the centromeres” is an event of mitotic anaphase.

items.q: Which of these is NOT an event of telophase?
c: sister chromatids moving to opposite poles
items.e: “Sister chromatids moving to opposite poles” is not an event of telophase; the other three are.

items.q: In which stage of meiosis does this happen: crossing over takes place at recombination nodules?
items.e: Pachytene: crossing over takes place at recombination nodules.

items.q: In which stage of meiosis does this happen: the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata are seen?
items.e: Diplotene: the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata are seen.

items.q: What happens in anaphase I of meiosis?
c: chiasmata terminalise and the nuclear envelope breaks down
homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together
crossing over takes place at recombination nodules
homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents
items.e: Anaphase I: homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together.

items.q: How many chromatids are present in a bivalent?
items.e: A bivalent is a pair of homologous chromosomes, each with two chromatids.

items.q: What happens in diplotene of meiosis?
c: homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together
the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata are seen
homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents
chiasmata terminalise and the nuclear envelope breaks down
items.e: Diplotene: the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata are seen.

items.q: Which of these is NOT an event of interphase?
items.e: “Crossing over” is not an event of interphase; the other three are.

items.q: How does cytokinesis happen in plant cells?
c: a furrow forms from the outside
a cell plate forms in the middle and grows outward
items.e: Animal cells form a cleavage furrow.

items.q: What happens in zygotene of meiosis?
c: homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents
sister chromatids separate as the centromere splits
homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together
crossing over takes place at recombination nodules
items.e: Zygotene: homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents.

items.q: Which of these is NOT an event of prophase I of meiosis?
items.e: “Duplication of the centriole” is not an event of prophase I of meiosis; the other three are.

items.q: In which stage of meiosis does this happen: homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents?
items.e: Zygotene: homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents.

items.q: A species has 5 pairs of chromosomes. How many different chromosome combinations can occur in zygotes from random fertilisation (ignoring crossing over)?
A diploid cell of an animal has 12 chromosomes. How many different combinations of chromosomes can its gametes have by independent segregation?
items.e: With n = 6 pairs, combinations = 2n = 64.

items.q: A diploid cell of a plant has 24 chromosomes. How many different combinations of chromosomes can its gametes have by independent segregation?
items.e: With n = 12 pairs, combinations = 2n = 4,096.

items.q: A species has 6 pairs of chromosomes. How many different chromosome combinations can occur in zygotes from random fertilisation (ignoring crossing over)?
A diploid body cell of a fungus has 14 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in one of its gametes?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: 7.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 24 hours. In a sample, 45 of 500 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 45/500 × 1,440 min = 130 min.

items.q: A species has 7 pairs of chromosomes. How many different chromosome combinations can occur in zygotes from random fertilisation (ignoring crossing over)?
A gamete of a species of fruit fly has 2 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in a cell after mitosis in this organism?
